question: Looking back at your completed task, how did you decide what to read or request next, and when you had enough information to answer? Give a brief account of observable choices and the information you expected further reads to provide.
answer: I began with the assigned guide, then tried broad discovery searches. They did not identify the style data, so I used the vocabulary index, which pointed to the style-choices and style-tiers resources. I requested both in the assigned HAL representation. The style-choices response supplied complete scope, Boolean property sets, conflict groups, every choice's option/value/tier, and an embedded tier vocabulary with descriptions. That was enough to join the five qualifying choices and interpret omissions for known IDs. I read the standalone tiers to confirm the descriptions and the linked contract to check map cardinality and coverage; those reads corroborated the answer but added no required task fact. I stopped because the complete local data answered the requested joins and groups, while no returned data specified invocation behavior.
